chain - -h

    [no]  this branch is a governed cycle
          It is not a cycle branch - cycle/<id>/plan, build, build-unattended or
          forward - so there is no intent, spec or plan

          date, a 24-hour time and seconds, as in 20260929_1456_32.

  The chain does not hold, because there is no chain.

  Two ways on, and they are not the same thing:

    Open the change as a cycle. Every change to what the solution does runs
    the full chain, a revert included, and a small change makes a short
    intent, spec and plan rather than none.

    Or decide, as a team, that this class of branch is exempt - and say so
    in branch policy by not requiring this check on it. That is a choice to
    accept ungoverned changes of that kind, which is yours to make. It is
    not the same as deleting this step, which accepts them everywhere and
    leaves nothing saying so.

  Moving to another sdlc release, or moving dependency versions, needs
  neither. A pull request that changes only the pin, what 'sdlc init' then
  writes, answers in the declared stack to what the release asks, and the
  versions in Directory.Packages.props, global.json or the tool manifest is
  checked without a cycle, given --base. Anything else in it - one source
  file or one package added - and it lands here.
